newsitem.title: UK: Brady bond prices lower following U.S. CPI report.
newsitem.headline: Brady bond prices lower following U.S. CPI report.

text.p: Brady bond prices were softer across the board on Thursday in line with U.S. Treasuries following a 0.1 percent rise in the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) in April, market experts said.

"There was an initial selloff but people will be looking next at cap use (capacity utilization) and industrial production," said one market analyst in London. Market sources said participants were also keeping a close watch on movements in the dollar/yen.

"People are watching closely what is going on in dollar/yen vis a vis the (30-year U.S. Treasury) bond because the bond has been coming off as dollar/yen broke 116," said one emerging market trader at a European bank.
At 1248 GMT, the benchmark U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was off 24/32 at 95.31 yielding 6.95 percent and the yen was at 116.02 against the dollar.
Growing concerns the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may raise its official discount rate, currently 0.50 percent, may also pressure prices of dollar-denominated assets longer-term.

The bearish tone in the emerging debt market was exacerbated by uncertainty over whether the Federal Reserve will move to further tighten U.S. monetary policy on May 20 when the Federal Market Open Committee (FOMC) convenes.

In the Latin Brady market, Brazilian Brady bonds continued to trend lower but traders said the country's "C" bonds were starting to look attractive at current levels with yield spreads nearing 500 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Bribery allegations reported in a Brazilian daily on Tuesday sparked a sharp selloff in the country's Brady bonds, with its "C" bonds falling by more than two percentage points in the last two days. Currently, "C" bonds were 3/4 lower at 75-1/8 bid.

Folha de Sao Paulo published what it said were transcripts of secretly taped conversations that revealed five congressmen may have taken bribes to vote for a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election.
The paper also reported on Wednesday that Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta may have supplied some of the money.
Motta denied involvement in the alledged scheme.
AMong Eastern European Bradys, Bulgarian IABs were 1/8 softer at 65-5/8 and Russian dollar-denominated Vnesheconombank loans were 1/2 lower at 83-3/8 bid.
